description: Composite subjects, role and group definitions, role assignment cardinality, and how the permissions of several roles combine and are explained. See spec/README.md for the format.

composites.name: any source permits, and a deny rule only limits the source that holds it
a composite that no source permits reports DENIED if some source explicitly denies
a composite with no sources permits nothing
the context is passed through, and each source applies its own policy
a source that cannot explain itself is reported with its answer only
an opaque source next to an explaining one makes the explanation partial
a failing source after the one that permits is left out; one the check reaches fails the check
a failing source consulted before any permit fails the check
composites nest, each reporting its own sources
malformed checks are rejected before any source is asked

scenarios.name: an exclusive group swaps one role for another with REPLACE_EXISTING
REJECT keeps the roles the target has

expect.reason: role group 'team' allows at most 2 role(s) and the target already holds 2

scenarios.name: REPLACE_OLDEST makes room by removing the longest-held role
REPLACE_NEWEST makes room by removing the most recently assigned role
REPLACE_EXISTING in a larger group removes every held role of the group
a group minimum rejects the unassignment that would go under it

expect.reason: role group 'tier' requires at least 1 role(s); unassigning would leave 0
role group 'tier' requires at least 1 role(s) in context academy:1; unassigning would leave 0

scenarios.name: group limits are counted per context, and roles without a context as one more context

expect.reason: role group 'school' allows at most 1 role(s) and the target already holds 1

scenarios.name: a replacement only removes roles held in the context being assigned in
roles without a group are never limited
two definitions of one group id fail the call and change nothing
an assignment policy that breaks the group's limits fails the call and changes nothing
a role is identified by its id: a second definition of a held id is NO_CHANGE and keeps the first
ALLOW_OVERRIDES and DENY_OVERRIDES differ only when one role denies what another permits
context first: a role held in the checked context decides before roles held without one
context first, reversed: a role held in the context re-allows what a global role denies
EXACT: a role assigned without a context does not apply inside one
a role built from rules answers only checks without a context
a role backed by a subject is asked without a context, and counted only by whether it permits
a role backed by a subject that cannot explain itself makes the explanation partial
a custom resolution policy is explained with its answer and the roles, none decisive
a failing role the check does not reach is left out; one it reaches fails the check
a target with no roles is permitted nothing, and malformed input is rejected
